title: Papyrus on Amazon Alexa: a published skill for every site
description:
Requested by Ryan (2026-10-31): put Papyrus on Amazon Alexa, built the way a real, published, certified skill has to be built, so it works on our two Echo Shows and on anyone else's.

Goal: a person says "Alexa, open <publication>" and hears and sees the latest stories. Echo Show devices show them on screen. A person who links their account gets the signed-in experience: their own reference feed, and Accept/Reject votes that train the site's Cyclotron.

Decisions in this plan (change them here if Ryan disagrees):
- One skill per Papyrus site, generated from site config, with the publication as the invocation name. This follows the config-only-per-site rule and each site's own Cognito pool. Pilot site: Pilobolus (pre-production). Anth.us goes last.
- The skill is a Papyrus plugin (amplify/plugins/alexa), like newsletter and reader-steering: a Lambda endpoint in the site backend, off unless the site turns it on.
- Sign-in uses Alexa's standard OAuth account linking (authorization code grant + PKCE) against a new Alexa app client on the site's Cognito pool. The Google provider is the only one. When a request needs a linked account, an Echo Show shows Amazon's own QR code, so the "scan to sign in" experience needs no custom flow. The CLI remote-login broker is not reused: certification expects standard account linking.
- Readers can use the public parts without linking. Account linking is optional, not mandatory.
- The skill package (manifest, interaction model, APL documents) lives in Git and ships through the pipeline. Nobody edits it by hand in the developer console.

Milestones (one epic each, in order):
1. Skill foundation: voice-only public stories, in development stage on our own Echos.
2. Echo Show screens: APL feed and story views.
3. Account linking: Cognito Alexa client, Google sign-in, QR linking on the Show.
4. Signed-in newsroom: personal reference feed and voice Accept/Reject votes.
5. Certification and publishing: pass Amazon review and go live for the pilot site.
6. Rollout to every site: config-only, Anth.us last.
7. Listen to full stories: long-form audio playback (follow-up after the first publication).

Ryan's own steps (I can't do these): own the Amazon Developer account and authorise the ASK CLI once for CI; approve the Cognito and backend deploys; create a dedicated Google test account for Amazon's certification testers (never a Cognito password user); submit for certification if the console requires the account owner.

Sources: developer.amazon.com account-linking requirements (updated 2026-02-04) and "How users experience account linking" (QR code on screen devices).

Every behaviour change ships with Gherkin specs. The last task is a p.apyr.us docs page.
